items.title: Unitree Soars Over 600% in Shanghai IPO, Cements China’s Lead in Humanoid Hardware
items.summary: Unitree Robotics debuted on the Shanghai STAR Market, with its shares soaring by up to 629%. The company is highly vertically integrated, producing 86% of its bill of materials in-house, which enables margins of around 60%. Unitree has partnered with AI developer DeepSeek to develop embodied intelligence models, aiming to solve the industry's software bottlenecks. The public listing highlights China's aggressive push to dominate humanoid robotics, contrasting with recent US import bans targeting Chinese robotics.
items.audio_script: From Humanoids Daily, "Unitree Soars Over 600% in Shanghai IPO, Cements China’s Lead in Humanoid Hardware." Unitree Robotics made its highly anticipated public listing on the Shanghai STAR Market, with its shares skyrocketing by as much as 629%. The company's strong vertical integration is evident, as 86% of its bill of materials are produced in-house, resulting in margins of approximately 60%. This achievement demonstrates Unitree's ability to manage its production and supply chain efficiently, a key factor in its rapid growth. The company's partnership with AI developer DeepSeek to develop embodied intelligence models is also noteworthy, as it aims to address the industry's software bottlenecks. This strategic collaboration further solidifies Unitree's position as a leader in humanoid robotics. The public listing marks a significant milestone in China's push to dominate the humanoid robotics market, contrasting with recent US import bans targeting Chinese robotics companies.

items.title: Hexagon starts training AEON humanoid robots at Schaeffler factories
items.summary: Hexagon Robotics and Schaeffler announce the next milestone in their collaboration, with AEON humanoid robots starting training at Schaeffler's Humanoid Gym in Germany. The gym provides a dedicated industrial environment for teaching AEON new industrial capabilities, building expertise, and expanding use cases on the factory floor. AEON will learn through imitation learning and repeated execution, refining and validating robot policies using representative manufacturing applications from Schaeffler's factories. The initiative supports the industrial deployment of AEON and expands the breadth of use cases on the factory floor.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Hexagon starts training AEON humanoid robots at Schaeffler factories". Hexagon Robotics and Schaeffler have announced a significant milestone in their collaboration, with the commencement of training for AEON humanoid robots at Schaeffler's Humanoid Gym in Germany. The AEON robots will learn new industrial capabilities by imitating and repeating tasks, with a focus on refining and validating robot policies through representative manufacturing applications from Schaeffler's factories. This training environment provides a dedicated industrial setting, allowing AEON to build expertise and expand its use cases on the factory floor. The initiative is expected to support the industrial deployment of AEON and further broaden its application in manufacturing settings.

items.title: VUB leads European project teaching soft robots to sense, repair and adapt
items.summary: Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) leads a European research project, RESSORT, to develop soft robots that can sense, repair and adapt. The four-year project combines breakthrough technologies, including self-healing materials, variable-stiffness structures, affordable tactile sensors, and artificial intelligence. The goal is to make soft robots more sustainable, reliable, and suitable for real-world applications in healthcare, the food industry, and industrial inspection.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "VUB leads European project teaching soft robots to sense, repair and adapt." VUB is leading a four-year European research project, RESSORT, aimed at developing soft robots capable of sensing, repairing and adapting. The project has successfully combined breakthrough technologies, including self-healing materials, variable-stiffness structures, affordable tactile sensors, and artificial intelligence. By integrating these advanced technologies, researchers have made significant progress in creating soft robots that can learn from their environment, adapt to new situations, and perform tasks more efficiently. The goal of RESSORT is to make soft robots more sustainable, reliable, and suitable for real-world applications in healthcare, the food industry, and industrial inspection. The project's findings demonstrate the potential for soft robots to improve efficiency and effectiveness in these fields.

items.title: Scientists combine EIT and pneumatic sensing for humanoid robot skin
items.summary: Scientists have developed a hybrid robotic skin that combines electrical impedance tomography and pneumatic pressure sensing to improve force detection across large areas of a humanoid robot. The system uses EIT to determine where contact occurs, while four sealed pneumatic pads provide an estimate of the force being applied. The hybrid sensing method reduces sensitivity variation by 43% compared to EIT alone.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Scientists combine EIT and pneumatic sensing for humanoid robot skin". The hybrid sensing method allows for reduced sensitivity variation, resulting in a 43% decrease compared to EIT alone. This innovative approach enables more accurate and reliable force detection, enhancing the overall performance of humanoid robots in various applications.

items.title: Faraday Future’s RoboShare takes first paid robot rental order
items.summary: Faraday Future Intelligent Electric announced its support for AIxC Holdings' orderly exit from its digital asset treasury strategy. AIxC will focus on physical AI and robot sharing and rental, with Faraday Future Intelligent Electric providing strategic, product, technology, business, and capital-market support through its "Four-Core Full-Stack AI" ecosystem. RoboShare, AIxC's robot-sharing and rental platform, completed its first paid commercial order, generating initial revenue for the platform. The platform's first customer is DU$TY, a Los Angeles-based artist and rapper.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: ROS Keeps Evolving via Physical AI SIG
items.summary: A blog post was published by OSRA in collaboration with its Special Interest Group on Physical AI (SIG PAI), detailing their efforts to evolve ROS. The SIG PAI aims to leverage ROS's strengths with complementary tools for Physical AI, addressing the rapid emergence of new tools for robotics. The post discusses their roadmap and ways for community involvement. ROS's future will incorporate both its existing capabilities and new tools for Physical AI.
items.audio_script:
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: ROS Keeps Evolving via Physical AI SIG". ROS is undergoing a significant evolution, driven by the collaboration between OSRA and its Special Interest Group on Physical AI, aimed at leveraging ROS's strengths with complementary tools for Physical AI to address the rapid emergence of new tools for robotics.

This effort has resulted in the publication of a blog post detailing the SIG PAI's roadmap and ways for community involvement, outlining the integration of new tools for Physical AI into ROS's existing capabilities. The SIG PAI has established a framework for community engagement, encouraging users to share their experiences and provide feedback on the evolving ROS framework. The SIG PAI's work will facilitate a seamless transition of ROS to incorporate both its current strengths and emerging tools for Physical AI.

This development is significant for the AI and robotics industry, as ROS continues to expand its capabilities, ensuring a strong foundation for future innovation and collaboration in the field of Physical AI.

items.title: Opinion: How robots are learning to navigate the building site
items.summary: Autonomous robots are being developed to navigate construction sites without relying on GPS, using Simultaneous Localisation and Mapping (SLAM) technology. SLAM builds a map of the environment using cameras or Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) sensors, combining localization and mapping to create a living map that adapts to the changing site. While SLAM has the potential to improve safety, productivity, and error reduction on construction sites, it is not a drop-in replacement for current methods and is subject to challenges such as airborne dust, physical debris, and integration with existing site management software.

The research demonstrates a promising approach to enabling robots to navigate complex environments on their own.

items.title: Rodriguez launches Movotrak ‘seventh axis’ for cobots
items.summary: Rodriguez has introduced the Movotrak Cobot Transfer Unit (CTU), a "seventh axis" system that allows a cobot to move between multiple workstations and extend its operating range to 10 meters. The system enables a single cobot to perform tasks at different positions along a production line, increasing robot utilisation and reducing repositioning requirements. The CTU includes integrated collision detection, which detects collisions while the carriage is moving and automatically stops its motion. The system can be installed horizontally or mounted on a wall or ceiling, making it suitable for applications such as machine tending and inspection.

items.title: A3 and Mahoning County expand access to free robotics training in Ohio through $500,000 workforce grant
items.summary: A3 and Mahoning County Career & Technical Center will offer no-cost robotics and automation training across Ohio through a $499,000 workforce grant. The grant will support approximately 3,000 individual course enrollments through June 30, 2027, and is part of Ohio's Individual Microcredential Assistance Program. The training program will cover topics such as industrial robotics, robot safety, and mobile robot safety, and is available to Ohio residents at no cost through the A3 website.

The training program, available through the A3 website, will cover topics such as industrial robotics, robot safety, and mobile robot safety. By expanding access to free robotics training, this initiative aims to equip Ohio residents with the skills needed to succeed in the industry.

items.title: Drones With Claws Perch on Arctic Icebergs
items.summary: Researchers have developed a drone called Ice Dart, equipped with spiny feet and shock-absorbing legs that enable it to perch on steep, slippery icebergs in the Arctic. The drone can latch onto glaciers and drifting icebergs, allowing for long-term monitoring of these areas. Ice Dart's design enables it to withstand the harsh Arctic environment and provide valuable insights into the region's climate and ecosystem.
items.audio_script: From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Drones With Claws Perch on Arctic Icebergs," researchers have developed a drone called Ice Dart, which features spiny feet and shock-absorbing legs that allow it to perch on steep, slippery icebergs in the Arctic, enabling long-term monitoring of glaciers and drifting icebergs. The development of Ice Dart was accomplished through a combination of robotics and materials science expertise, with the team leveraging 3D printing to create the drone's unique foot structure and testing its capabilities in controlled Arctic environments. The drone's design enables it to withstand the harsh Arctic conditions, providing valuable insights into the region's climate and ecosystem.

items.title: Autonomous drones and the future of war in an AI-driven world | Letter
items.summary: Autonomous drones are already being used in warfare, killing civilians and combatants without distinction. Experts argue that losing control of AI systems, including drones, poses a significant risk to humanity. To prevent rogue AI, military surgeon Dr. Darren Mann suggests that humans must be able to check and audit the decisions made by autonomous systems, rather than relying on opaque intelligence.
items.audio_script: From The Guardian - Artificial Intelligence, "Autonomous drones and the future of war in an AI-driven world | Letter", it has been reported that autonomous drones are already being used in warfare, resulting in the killing of civilians and combatants without distinction, highlighting the need for humans to regain control over AI systems. According to Dr. Darren Mann, a military surgeon, the lack of transparency in AI decision-making poses a significant risk to humanity, and experts argue that humans must be able to check and audit the decisions made by autonomous systems. The letter suggests that this is crucial to prevent rogue AI, and Dr. Mann's proposal emphasizes the need for a more transparent and accountable approach to AI development.

items.title: Galbot Teases ET1 Bipedal Humanoid Ahead of WRC 2026 Debut
items.summary: Galbot has previewed the ET1, its first fully bipedal humanoid robot, ahead of its debut at WRC 2026 in Beijing, showcasing dynamic athletic capabilities in a CGI teaser. The ET1 marks a significant architectural pivot from Galbot's commercial G1 platform, as the company eyes a potential $4 billion IPO. The robot's tennis demonstration builds on Galbot's LATENT athletic framework, a research initiative that aims to teach robots athletic tennis skills from fragmented motion capture data.

The ET1's dynamic athletic capabilities were showcased, building on Galbot's LATENT athletic framework, a research initiative that aimed to teach robots athletic tennis skills from fragmented motion capture data, resulting in a successful tennis demonstration.

items.title: Warehouse robotics company Brightpick expands partnership with Dr. Max Group
items.summary: Brightpick, a provider of AI-powered warehouse automation, is expanding its partnership with Dr. Max Group, Europe's largest pharmacy chain, to deploy an additional 44 Autopicker autonomous mobile robots across three facilities in the Czech Republic and Slovakia. The total number of deployed robots will reach 74 units, improving operational efficiency and reducing manual picking labor by 95%. The deployment will also increase warehouse capacity and eliminate picking errors. Two new projects will be completed in the second half of this year.

items.title: FetchMan: Learning Visual Humanoid Loco-Manipulation Policies from Simulated Experiences
items.summary: Researchers developed FetchMan, a policy learning approach that enables visual humanoid loco-manipulation policies to generalize to novel scenes and objects. By learning from simulated data and refining the cloned policy with Flow-GRPO, FetchMan achieves performance that synthetic behavior cloning cannot match. On a real Unitree G1, FetchMan's single-object reach-and-pick policy achieves 73.3% success. The researchers extend this approach to multi-object training, a step toward creating generalist policies.

items.title: Lambda-Hold Control: Human-Like Movement Emerges from a Minimal Task Reward in Predictive Musculoskeletal Simulation
items.summary: A minimal task reward enables a muscle-actuated skeletal model to learn human-like sprinting, emerging from a predictive musculoskeletal simulation with the proposed $\lambda$-hold controller. The controller, grounded in physiology, enables efficient exploration through an equilibrium-point threshold length $\lambda$, reducing the frequency of querying. The $\lambda$-hold controller enables a muscle-actuated skeletal model to learn human-like behavior in an hour of training, contributing to developing a learnable model of the human motor controller.

items.title: Terrain-Aware Local Path Planning with Global DEM Data Integration for Autonomous UGV Navigation
items.summary: Researchers have proposed a hybrid framework that integrates low-resolution Digital Elevation Model (DEM) data with real-time LiDAR-based obstacle detection and terrain analysis for efficient path planning in autonomous unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs). A global path is initially computed using a preprocessed DEM-based A* algorithm, and subsequently, local sensor data drives adaptive path correction to enable the UGV to navigate sudden environmental changes while maintaining safety and efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate significant improvements over a baseline approach, achieving a 95% obstacle avoidance rate and reducing the average encountered slope from $8^\circ$ to $2.7^\circ$ in custom terrain.

items.title: PDDL-ART: Autonomous Symbolic Abstraction From Demonstration For Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation Using Vision-Language Models
items.summary: PDDL-ART autonomously generates task-specific PDDL domain and problem descriptions from a single expert demonstration, natural language task description, and a library of available high-level action names, achieving an average success rate of 93.3% in manipulation tasks. The framework uses a multi-stage correction pipeline operating at syntactic, semantic, and execution levels, incorporating geometric and temporal reasoning for evaluating relational predicates.

items.title: Teach and Grow: An Agent-Centered Architecture for General Robot Learning
items.summary: Teach-and-Grow Learning (TGL) is an agent-centered architecture for general robot learning that enables robots to acquire new skills without retraining. In its general form, a multimodal agent turns a few successful demonstrations into reusable Skill Blocks, which are then composed to achieve meaningful subgoals. A Skill Library stores executable behavior, while structured Experience Memory carries forward success, failure, and repair. LIBERO evaluation attains state-of-the-art performance, with controlled studies showing skill induction, persistent reuse, and agent-directed adaptation.

items.title: Robust Brachiation on a Life-Sized Dual-Arm Robot Using Waypoint-Guided Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Researchers developed a reinforcement learning-based method to achieve robust brachiation on a life-sized dual-arm robot using Waypoint-Guided Reinforcement Learning (WGRL). WGRL guides behavior acquisition by sparsely specifying waypoints for the end-effector trajectory, while whole-body motion is generated through reinforcement learning. The proposed method achieves both forward progression and motion stability, and is evaluated through Sim-to-Sim experiments and hardware experiments.

items.title: ORPA: Online Residual Policy Adaptation for Robot Manipulation Control with Human Feedback
items.summary: ORPA, a framework for immediate, feedback-driven correction of robot actions, augments a pretrained control policy with a lightweight, feedback-conditioned module that predicts residual adjustments in joint space. This allows the system to adapt its behavior at runtime. ORPA is evaluated on precision-sensitive manipulation tasks using the ALOHA platform, demonstrating improvements in success rate and recovery from small perturbations. ORPA outperforms baseline control policies and rule-based inverse kinematics corrections.

items.title: Reconfiguration-Complete Motion Primitives with Constructive Planning for Deformable Planar Modular Robots
items.summary: Researchers Jie Gu and six others introduced a square-cell abstraction to map deformable rhombus modules to fixed-size grid cells, enabling the definition of reconfiguration planning and analysis for modular robots. The abstraction introduces two primitives, pivoting and shearing, which allow for the transformation of any non-straight edge-connected configuration with 7 or more modules to a fixed canonical staircase. The staircase-canonicalization planner is constructive and preserves connectivity, and a boundary-to-delivery lookahead selector reduces planning time. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the new framework, which outperforms prior frameworks.

items.title: MANIGUARD: A Benchmark and Data Suite for Specification-Grounded Safety Evaluation and Improvement of Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: ManiGuard is a specification-grounded framework for evaluating and improving the safety of foundation-model manipulation in robotics. It includes a benchmark suite, ManiGuard-Bench, which organizes tasks into 200 locked base tasks and provides 1,000 scenarios with safety specifications fixed. Evaluating safety independently of task success is crucial, as 6-21% of successful rollouts violate the specification.
